sections.title: Understanding the Problem
points: Search a large corpus of social posts by keyword and order results by recency or popularity.
Posting and liking update the primary data; a derived search index supports query patterns the primary store cannot serve efficiently.

sections.title: Functional Requirements
points: Create and like posts.
Search by keyword, with multi-keyword and phrase searches as deeper requirements.
Sort results by recency or like count and paginate them.

sections.title: Non-functional Requirements
points: Keep queries fast over a very large corpus and accept bounded indexing delay.
Handle high post and like write volume, including popular terms and posts.
Preserve visibility and deletion rules even when the search index or caches lag.

sections.title: Core Entities
points: Post stores author, text, creation time, visibility, and authoritative like information.
TermPosting maps a normalized term to matching document IDs and optional positions.
SearchDocument stores fields needed for filtering and sorting; indexing progress tracks source changes.

sections.title: API
points: Create a post and like or unlike it through authenticated write APIs.
Search with query text, sort order, filters, limit, and a stable continuation cursor.
Return post summaries and enforce access controls before exposing restricted content.

sections.title: 1) Writes and indexing
points: Persist posts and likes in the primary system, then publish change events reliably.
Indexing workers tokenize text and update a derived inverted index.
Track indexing versions so delayed updates cannot overwrite newer content or resurrect deleted posts.

flows.title: Publish a post into the search index
steps: The author creates or edits a post through the primary post service, which commits content, visibility, and a version.
A reliable change stream or outbox publishes that committed version to indexing workers.
The worker tokenizes the text, computes searchable fields, and writes the search document and postings for the stable post ID.
Version checks prevent a delayed old update from replacing newer content or undoing a deletion.
After the search engine's refresh boundary, queries can discover the updated document; primary write acknowledgement can occur before that search visibility.

sections.title: 2) Keyword retrieval
points: Full table scans are unsuitable for frequent keyword searches across a large corpus.
An inverted index maps each term to a posting list of matching post IDs.
Partition the index and coordinate queries across relevant shards, merging bounded result sets.
Hydrate selected results from stored search fields or batched primary/cache reads.

flows.title: Execute a keyword or phrase search
steps: The client sends query text, filters, sort mode, and continuation data to the search coordinator.
The coordinator normalizes the query and routes it to the relevant search shards.
Each shard retrieves term postings, intersects or unions candidates, and checks positions for phrase requirements.
Shards apply supported filters and return bounded locally ranked candidates with stable sort values.
The coordinator merges candidates, deduplicates results, and enforces current visibility where stale index data could expose restricted content.
It hydrates the selected page and returns a cursor containing the ordering context, avoiding a full-corpus scan or unbounded result transfer.

sections.title: 3) Sorting
points: Recency ordering can exploit timestamps and time-partitioned data.
Popularity ordering requires maintaining sortable like counts or ranking structures as likes arrive.
Return stable tie-breakers in cursors because equal timestamps or counts are common.

sections.title: 1) Read scale
points: Replicate query capacity and cache popular queries or posting-list fragments where freshness allows.
A popular term can touch enormous posting lists; bound candidate work and avoid transferring every match to a coordinator.
Include filters, sort mode, and relevant visibility scope in cache keys.

sections.title: 2) Multiple terms and phrases
points: AND queries intersect posting lists; OR queries union them.
Process selective terms first to reduce intermediate candidates.
Phrase queries need term positions or a verification phase; matching all words alone does not prove adjacency or order.

sections.title: 3) Write scale
points: Batch indexing updates and separate post creation from frequent like-count changes.
Popularity updates can be coalesced when a small ranking delay is acceptable.
Keep durable change streams so rebuilding or resharding the index does not lose concurrent writes.
Apply deletions and permission changes reliably; stale index entries must not bypass final visibility checks.

sections.title: 4) Storage efficiency
points: Compress sorted posting lists, use compact document IDs, and avoid duplicating fields that are not needed for search.
Partition old data by time and use retention or tiered storage according to product requirements.
Index size, query fanout, and update cost should drive the choice of a specialized search engine versus custom infrastructure.

sections.title: Final Design
points: Primary post storage feeds a versioned, replayable indexing pipeline.
Sharded inverted indexes and sortable metadata support retrieval, while query replicas and caches serve reads.
Batched popularity updates, compressed postings, and explicit visibility checks control cost without sacrificing access correctness.
